title: Weil conjectures III: Riemann hypothesis
statement:
Fix a finite field
$k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, with algebraic closure
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$.
Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper and geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\geq0$, and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$.
Let $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$, $0\leq i\leq2d$, be the
integral Frobenius factors
provided by [thm-weil-final-integrality]: $P_i(0)=1$, and for
every $\ell\neq p$,

$$
P_i^{(\ell)}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid H^i(X,\mathbf Q_\ell)),
$$

where $F_{i,\ell}$ is
geometric Frobenius
on ordinary cohomology,
and $P_i^{(\ell)}$ means coefficientwise extension
$\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Q_\ell$.
For every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, put
$r_i=\deg P_i$ and $P_i^\#(U)=U^{r_i}P_i(U^{-1})$. A
reciprocal root
$\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ means a root of $P_i^\#$; put
$\beta=\alpha^{-1}$, the corresponding
ordinary root. Every
reciprocal root $\alpha$ is a
algebraic integer and a
Weil number for $q$ of weight $i$:

$$
|\tau(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}
$$

for every embedding $\tau:\mathbf Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$. Then
$|\tau(\beta)|=q^{-i/2}$ for every embedding
$\tau:\mathbf Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$.

proof.text:
*Step 1: the objects of the statement are those of [prop-arithmetic-roots].* The finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, with $q=p^a$, and its fixed algebraic closure $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ are the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]; the hypotheses on $X_0$ (smooth of pure dimension $d\geq0$, proper, geometrically connected) are those of [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses]; $X=X_0	imes_{k_0}k$ is the geometric fiber of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For every prime $\ell
eq p$, $H^i(X,\mathbf Q_\ell)$ is the ordinary cohomology group of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] and $F_{i,\ell}$ the geometric Frobenius of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] on it; by [def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family] these are $V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql)$ and $F_{i,\ell}=F_\ell|_{V_{i,\ell}}$, and $\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid H^i(X,\mathbf Q_\ell))$, the reverse characteristic polynomial of [def-weil-reverse-characteristic-polynomial], is the determinant factor $P_{i,\ell}(T)\in\Ql[T]$ of that family. The polynomials $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$ ([def-weil-polynomial-ring]) are those provided by Theorem [thm-weil-final-integrality] for $X_0$: for each $0\leq i\leq2d$, $P_i$ is the unique polynomial with $P_i(0)=1$ whose coefficientwise extension $P_i^{(\ell)}\in\Ql[T]$ ([def-weil-coefficientwise-extension]) equals $\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid H^i(X,\Ql))$ for every prime $\ell
eq p$. Hence $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ for every $\ell
eq p$: $P_i$ is an integral realization-independent factor in degree $i$ in the sense of [def-weil-integral-frobenius-factor], with $P_i(0)=1$. Fix an integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$ and put $r_i=\deg P_i$ ([def-weil-polynomial-ring]). The statement takes its roots $\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ in an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q$ fixed once and for all ([def-weil-algebraic-closure]; the same fixed $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ as in [def-weil-numbers]). These are exactly the data and hypotheses of [prop-arithmetic-roots]: the datum, $X_0$ and $X$, the indeterminates $T$ and $U$, the coefficientwise extension $P^{(\ell)}$, the cohomological family $(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})$, the integer $i$, the integral Frobenius factor $P_i$ with $P_i(0)=1$ and $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ for every $\ell
eq p$, $r_i=\deg P_i$, and the fixed $\overline{\mathbf Q}$. (Deligne states the same objects: the characteristic polynomial of $F^*$ on $H^i(X,\Ql)$ has integer coefficients independent of $\ell$, which is Theorem [thm-weil-final-integrality]; the present theorem is the assertion on its complex roots.)

source.place: Théorème (1.6), p. 276 ('le polynôme caractéristique det(t·1 − F*, H^i(X,Q_ℓ)) est à coefficients entiers indépendants de ℓ'); blueprint literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-zeta-weil/sk-thm-weil3/thm-weil-final-rh.md ## Proof, 'The root/eigenvalue identification is [def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots]' and 'The arithmetic formulation ... [is] recorded in [prop-arithmetic-roots]'

proof.text: *Step 2: reciprocal roots.* The statement's conventions are those of [prop-arithmetic-roots], word for word: $P_i^\#(U)=U^{r_i}P_i(U^{-1})$, a reciprocal root $\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ is a root of $P_i^\#$, and $\beta=\alpha^{-1}$ is the corresponding ordinary root; by Step 1 of the proof of [prop-arithmetic-roots] (through [lem-weil-reciprocal-polynomial]) $P_i^\#\in\mathbf Z[U]$, every reciprocal root is nonzero, and the ordinary roots are exactly the roots of $P_i$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}$, so this is the convention of [def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots] with $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ in place of $\Qlb$. By Step 1, [prop-arithmetic-roots] applies to $X_0$, $i$ and $P_i$, and its conclusions are: $P_i^\#$ is monic; every reciprocal root $\alpha$ is an algebraic integer; for every embedding $\tau:\mathbf Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$, $|\tau(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$; and $\alpha$ is a $q$-Weil number of weight $i$. Here 'algebraic integer', '$q$-Weil number of weight $i$', $\mathbf Q(\alpha)$, the embeddings $\tau$ and $|\cdot|$ have the meaning of [def-weil-numbers], in [prop-arithmetic-roots] as in the present statement; and since every field homomorphism $\mathbf Q(\alpha)\to\mathbf C$ is the identity on $\mathbf Q$, 'every embedding $\tau:\mathbf Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$' is the set $\operatorname{Emb}_{\mathbf Q}(\mathbf Q(\alpha),\mathbf C)$ of that definition. This is the first assertion of the theorem: every reciprocal root $\alpha$ is an algebraic integer and a Weil number for $q$ of weight $i$, $|\tau(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$ for every $\tau$. (This is Deligne's (1.6): the complex roots $\alpha$ of $\det(t\cdot1-F^*,H^i(X,\Ql))$, the complex conjugates of the eigenvalues of $F^*$, have $|\alpha|=q^{i/2}$; his roots of $\det(t-F^*)$ are the reciprocal roots of $P_i(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell})$, and 'complex conjugates' are the images $\tau(\alpha)$ under all embeddings.)

source.place: Théorème (1.6), p. 276 ('Les racines complexes α de ce polynôme (les conjugués complexes des valeurs propres de F*) sont de valeur absolue |α| = q^{i/2}'); blueprint literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-zeta-weil/sk-thm-weil3/thm-weil-final-rh.md ## Proof, 'hence its roots are algebraic integers ... [prop-weight-purity-roots] gives |τ(α)|=q^{i/2}. In the terminology of [def-weil-numbers], this is precisely the q-Weil condition'

proof.text: *Step 3: ordinary roots.* Let $\beta$ be an ordinary root, that is, $\beta=\alpha^{-1}$ for a reciprocal root $\alpha$ (Step 2). The last clause of [prop-arithmetic-roots], for the same $X_0$, $i$, $P_i$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}$, states that for every embedding $\tau:\mathbf Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$ one has $|\tau(\beta)|=q^{-i/2}$, with the notation of [def-weil-numbers]. This is the 'Then' clause of the theorem. (Directly: $\mathbf Q(\beta)=\mathbf Q(\alpha)$ and $\tau(\beta)=\tau(\alpha)^{-1}$ for every $\tau$, so $|\tau(\beta)|=|\tau(\alpha)|^{-1}=q^{-i/2}$ by Step 2.)

split_report.summary: Statement checked against its master source (verbatim, kept, including the source's 'a algebraic integer'), against the slopmaster2 LaTeX clause (iii) of thm:weil-final (01_final_weil_conjectures.tex, lines 3608-3620; same assertion, stated for the canonical factors and without the det(1-TF) characterization, which the slopmaster2 text puts in clause (ii)), and against Deligne Weil I, Théorème (1.6), p. 276: Deligne's complex roots of det(t·1 − F*, H^i) are the reciprocal roots of P_i, and 'conjugués complexes' are the images under all embeddings, so the statement is his. The section sketch sk-thm-weil3 says the theorem 'is [sk-thm-rh]', whose node is the reviewed prop-arithmetic-roots, and the imported one-paragraph proof cited eight nodes without deriving anything from them, so it is replaced by three steps: identification of the statement's objects (datum, X, H^i, F_{i,l}, det(1-TF), P^{(l)}, the P_i of thm-weil-final-integrality) with the hypotheses of prop-arithmetic-roots, in particular P_i^{(l)}=P_{i,l} so that P_i is an integral Frobenius factor with P_i(0)=1; the reciprocal-root clause read off from prop-arithmetic-roots (same conventions for P_i^#, reciprocal and ordinary roots, algebraic integer, q-Weil number, Q(alpha), embeddings); and the ordinary-root clause from its last clause. Dropped from the direct proof: prop-integral-recovery (its content is already consumed by thm-weil-final-integrality, which the statement cites for the P_i), lem-embedding-extension and prop-weight-purity-roots (used inside prop-arithmetic-roots, steps 5-6), thm-weil-deligne-purity (reached through prop-weight-purity), and prop-weil-realization-independent-degrees (degree independence, which this theorem asserts nothing about; the blueprint cited it as 'also recorded'; after this change no target reaches it, its content being the degree clause of prop-integral-recovery and thm-weil-final-betti). Statement dependencies completed: the cohomological family, the reverse characteristic polynomial, coefficientwise extension, the polynomial ring and degree, the fixed algebraic closure of Q, the reciprocal/ordinary-root convention and the Weil-number/algebraic-integer notions; the imported six kept. No new node needed. Mathlib searched for the item: nothing beyond l-adic cohomology on the pro-étale site. The Lean on both branches (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.weil_conjectures, WeilConjectures/Statement.lean 86-98) states something else, the conjunction of all three Weil conjectures for an existentially quantified family P with no cohomological characterization; see the report.
